analysis.one_liner: LTM Limited (formerly LTIMindtree, renamed March 2026) is an IT and digital/AI consulting services company formed from the L&T Infotech-Mindtree merger, majority-owned by Larsen & Toubro.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (quarter to Sept 2026) were announced on 16 October 2026: revenue rose 13.6% YoY to roughly ₹11,808 crore with a 15.5% EBIT margin, but new deal bookings (TCV) fell to $1.26 billion from $1.68 billion the prior quarter as the company pivots toward shorter, faster-converting AI contracts instead of large multi-year deals. The board declared an interim dividend of ₹25/share with a record date of 23 October 2026 - about a week from now.
analysis.plain_terms: This company helps large businesses with IT systems, cloud and now AI-driven projects, and it sits inside the L&T group. Revenue is still growing at a healthy double-digit clip, but the pipeline of new deals signed this quarter shrank by roughly a quarter versus the previous one - a forward-looking warning sign even though the current quarter's numbers look fine. The tension is simple: today's growth looks solid, but the fuel for tomorrow's growth (new orders) is running lower.
analysis.quarters: Revenue: ~₹11,808 cr, +13.6% YoY, +2% QoQ. EBIT margin slipped slightly to 15.5% from 15.6% the prior quarter. PAT came in around ₹1,398 crore - sources disagree on whether this is flat or down ~5% YoY depending on which prior-year comparative base is used; this should be checked against the company's own exchange filing rather than taken at face value. Deal TCV fell from $1.68bn (Q1 FY27) and $1.59bn (Q2 FY26) to $1.26bn - management attributes this to a deliberate shift toward shorter AI-led deals rather than demand weakness, and flagged the Technology & Services vertical and Middle East/Saudi exposure as soft spots. AI-related revenue (Enterprise + Business AI) grew 47% YoY but is still only about 13% of total revenue - a fast growth rate off a small base, not yet a company-defining number.
analysis.performance_read: The uncomfortable fact first: this stock has been a serial underperformer. It is down 38.2% from its January 2022 peak of ₹7,106.64, with no stock splits or demergers to explain away any part of that fall - this is a real price decline, not a corporate-action illusion. Over 1 year it is down 20.56% versus the Nifty's -9.53% and peer Persistent Systems' -1.03%. Over 3 years it is down 12.16% while the Nifty gained 16.83% and Persistent Systems gained 104.87%. Over 5 years the gap is even starker: -20.72% for this stock versus +25.27% for the Nifty and +188.83% for Persistent Systems. By any measure, long-term holders have badly lagged both the market and the obvious peer.
analysis.valuation_read: At roughly 25-26x trailing earnings and about 5.3x book value, the stock is not statistically cheap - but it is well below where it traded before the 2022 peak, and well below where Persistent Systems has re-rated to. The 'why' is clear: the market has marked it down for weaker order bookings, margin pressure, and Middle East softness relative to faster-growing IT peers. The separate question of 'whether it is cheap' is harder to answer - a mid-20s P/E still prices in continued double-digit growth, which this quarter's falling deal TCV puts in some doubt.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is currently revenue-led - the top line is genuinely expanding (13.6% YoY), not just margin expansion on a flat base. But the forward indicator (new deal signings) fell sharply this quarter, and margin is edging down rather than up. AI revenue growth of 47% YoY sounds dramatic but is growth off a small base (about 13% of total revenue) and should not be read as transforming the overall growth rate yet.
analysis.health_read: Financial health looks solid: the company is reported to be essentially debt-free, with ROE near 22% and ROCE near 31%. As an IT services business it is asset-light, so profits converting into cash is typically not the concern here. The real risk is on the business side - client demand, deal pipeline, and competitive pressure in the AI-services pivot - not balance-sheet or leverage risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter Larsen & Toubro holds roughly 68.5-68.7% with no pledging reported, which gives strong strategic backing. FII holding is around 6.4-6.5%; DII holding is reported anywhere from roughly 12% to 17% depending on the source, and this range could not be reconciled with confidence - treat the DII figure as approximate. There is no disclosed stake from any well-known individual investor on the register; ownership here is essentially a promoter-plus-institutions story, not a 'famous investor' story.
strengths: Revenue grew 13.6% YoY to ~₹11,808 crore in Q2 FY27
Near debt-free balance sheet with ROCE around 31% and ROE around 22%
AI-linked revenue (Enterprise + Business AI) grew 47% YoY, now ~13% of total revenue
Strong promoter backing from Larsen & Toubro (~68.5% stake) with no pledging
watchpoints: Deal order inflow (TCV) fell to $1.26 billion from $1.68 billion the prior quarter, a ~25% sequential drop in new business signed
Stock has badly underperformed both the Nifty and peer Persistent Systems over 3 and 5 years (e.g., -12.16% vs peer's +104.87% over 3 years)
PAT growth versus the prior year is ambiguous across sources (flat to -5%) and needs verification against the company's own filing
Management flagged softness in the Technology & Services vertical and Middle East/Saudi exposure as near-term drags
analysis.one_thing: Whether deal TCV recovers in the next quarter or keeps falling - this tells you if the drop to $1.26 billion was a one-off from the shift to shorter AI deals, or the start of a genuine pipeline slowdown that would undercut the current double-digit revenue growth.
analysis.data_notes: Revenue, EBIT margin, the ₹25/share dividend and its 23 October 2026 record date, and recent deal news were corroborated across multiple independent sources. Two items are flagged as unresolved: the YoY PAT comparison base (sources differ on whether PAT was flat or down ~5%) and DII shareholding percentage (sources range from ~12% to ~17%) - both should be checked against the company's official exchange filing before being treated as final. Valuation ratios (P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE) are from financial aggregators rather than directly from company filings and should be treated as approximate.
